note: The legacy rendering is accurate but marked. Retention is justified by the rare critical term and its useful distinction from corporativismo.

register: Formal critical vocabulary for abusive use of people or resources; the same noun is neutral in established technical phrases such as explotación minera.
trap: Explotación can be abusive or neutral extraction in Spanish; do not replace the critical labour sense with the neutral aprovechamiento without context.
example_tl: La explotación laboral en las cadenas globales permanece invisible mientras las marcas externalizan la producción y publican compromisos sociales difíciles de verificar.
example_en: Labour exploitation in global supply chains remains invisible while brands outsource production and publish social commitments that are difficult to verify.
cloze: La {{c1::explotación laboral}} en las cadenas globales permanece invisible mientras las marcas externalizan la producción y publican compromisos sociales difíciles de verificar.
note: The old rendering is accurate but polysemous. Retention is justified by the critical labour sense and the need to separate it from neutral resource exploitation.

alts: el lucro abusivo obtenido con algo
register: Critical economic and journalistic vocabulary for exploiting scarcity or exceptional circumstances to obtain excessive profits.
trap: Profiteering is not ordinary rentabilidad or lucro: it entails taking unfair advantage of a situation, often through excessive prices.
example_tl: La especulación abusiva con medicamentos esenciales permitió a varios intermediarios multiplicar sus márgenes mientras los hospitales afrontaban una escasez evitable.
example_en: Profiteering from essential medicines allowed several intermediaries to multiply their margins while hospitals faced an avoidable shortage.
cloze: {{c1::La especulación abusiva con}} medicamentos esenciales permitió a varios intermediarios multiplicar sus márgenes mientras los hospitales afrontaban una escasez evitable.
note: Materially corrects old_back: lucrativismo is not the idiomatic Spanish term and fails to convey exploitation through excessive profit. Self-review selected a con complement to make the target frame production-ready.

register: Critical technology and political-theory term for treating complex social problems as if technical fixes alone could resolve them.
trap: Solucionismo is critical, unlike neutral orientación a la solución; it questions the reduction of political problems to technical design tasks.
example_tl: El solucionismo tecnológico reduce conflictos políticos complejos a fallos de diseño y desplaza preguntas incómodas sobre poder, intereses y responsabilidad democrática.
example_en: Technological solutionism reduces complex political conflicts to design flaws and displaces uncomfortable questions about power, interests and democratic accountability.
cloze: {{c1::El solucionismo tecnológico}} reduce conflictos políticos complejos a fallos de diseño y desplaza preguntas incómodas sobre poder, intereses y responsabilidad democrática.
note: Old_back has the correct base term but leaves the critical sense underspecified; tecnológico fixes the established concept intended in this topic.

register: Specialist financial-technology vocabulary for representing rights in an asset through digital tokens, particularly on distributed ledgers.
trap: Tokenización also names the segmentation of text in language processing; the complement is essential because the two technical senses are not interchangeable.
example_tl: La tokenización de activos promete ampliar el acceso a la inversión, pero también puede trasladar riesgos financieros a infraestructuras digitales poco supervisadas.
example_en: Asset tokenization promises to broaden access to investment, but it may also transfer financial risks to poorly supervised digital infrastructures.
cloze: {{c1::La tokenización de activos}} promete ampliar el acceso a la inversión, pero también puede trasladar riesgos financieros a infraestructuras digitales poco supervisadas.
note: The legacy term is valid but polysemous. This note deliberately selects the financial-asset sense rather than the language-processing sense.

register: Neutral-formal in media and technology criticism, often used critically for confidence that innovation will produce social progress by itself.
trap: Spanish writes the productive prefix tecno- joined to the base, without the English hyphen: tecnooptimismo, not *tecno-optimismo.
example_tl: El tecnooptimismo dominante presenta cada nueva infraestructura como progreso inevitable y relega sus costes laborales, ambientales y democráticos a simples efectos secundarios.
example_en: Dominant techno-optimism presents every new infrastructure as inevitable progress and relegates its labor, environmental and democratic costs to mere side effects.
cloze: {{c1::El tecnooptimismo}} dominante presenta cada nueva infraestructura como progreso inevitable y relega sus costes laborales, ambientales y democráticos a simples efectos secundarios.
note: Old_back identifies the right term but capitalizes a common noun; the note also makes the closed Spanish spelling explicit.

register: Neutral internet vocabulary, somewhat associated with early online culture but still useful for norms of respectful digital communication.
trap: Spanish adapts English netiquette as netiqueta, with one t and the productive ending -eta; the English spelling is unnecessary.
example_tl: La netiqueta profesional exige corregir información falsa sin humillar al interlocutor, especialmente cuando el debate público ya está marcado por la polarización.
example_en: Professional netiquette requires correcting false information without humiliating the other person, especially when public debate is already marked by polarization.
cloze: {{c1::La netiqueta}} profesional exige corregir información falsa sin humillar al interlocutor, especialmente cuando el debate público ya está marcado por la polarización.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; retention is justified by the adapted Spanish spelling.

register: Formal-critical institutional and legal vocabulary for acting beyond the powers, remit or limits legitimately assigned to an authority.
trap: The English noun is not *sobrealcance; extralimitación normally needs context identifying the authority, power or function whose limits were exceeded.
example_tl: La extralimitación del regulador debilitó una sentencia necesaria, pues el tribunal concluyó que había impuesto obligaciones sin respaldo legal suficiente.
example_en: The regulator's overreach weakened a necessary ruling, since the court concluded that it had imposed obligations without sufficient legal basis.
cloze: {{c1::La extralimitación}} del regulador debilitó una sentencia necesaria, pues el tribunal concluyó que había impuesto obligaciones sin respaldo legal suficiente.
note: Old_back supplies the correct noun but omits its article and institutional frame. Self-review narrowed the example to overreach of legal authority rather than generic excess.

register: Neutral technical and policy usage for software whose source code can be inspected, modified and redistributed under its licence.
trap: Before a Spanish noun, open-source is normally de código abierto, not an English-patterned compound such as *abierto-fuente.
example_tl: La administración eligió una plataforma de código abierto para poder auditar sus componentes, corregir vulnerabilidades y reducir la dependencia de un único proveedor.
example_en: The administration chose an open-source platform so it could audit its components, fix vulnerabilities and reduce dependence on a single provider.
cloze: La administración eligió una plataforma {{c1::de código abierto}} para poder auditar sus componentes, corregir vulnerabilidades y reducir la dependencia de un único proveedor.
note: Materially refines old_back: código abierto names the concept, while the source adjective requires the productive de código abierto construction.

register: Formal and often critical geopolitical metaphor for fragmentation into mutually hostile, isolated or incompatible units.
trap: Balcanización is stronger and more historically loaded than generic fragmentación; Spanish uses c and a written accent on the final ó.
example_tl: La balcanización de internet avanza cuando cada potencia impone estándares incompatibles y obliga a las empresas a duplicar infraestructuras, controles y servicios.
example_en: The balkanization of the internet advances when each power imposes incompatible standards and forces companies to duplicate infrastructures, controls and services.
cloze: {{c1::La balcanización de}} internet avanza cuando cada potencia impone estándares incompatibles y obliga a las empresas a duplicar infraestructuras, controles y servicios.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from capitalization. The exact-duplicate report does not assign this prompt to another topic; the note retains its distinctive rivalry implication.

register: Neutral-formal economics and competition-policy term for a market dominated by exactly two suppliers or platforms.
trap: Duopolio refers specifically to two dominant suppliers; oligopolio is broader and does not preserve that exact numerical distinction.
example_tl: El duopolio publicitario permite a dos plataformas fijar condiciones para los medios, aunque ninguna controle por sí sola todo el mercado.
example_en: The advertising duopoly allows two platforms to set terms for media outlets, although neither controls the entire market on its own.
cloze: {{c1::El duopolio}} publicitario permite a dos plataformas fijar condiciones para los medios, aunque ninguna controle por sí sola todo el mercado.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; retention is justified by the precise contrast with the broader oligopolio.

register: Neutral technical usage; cifrado is concise and widely used, while encriptación is also valid in computing and communications.
trap: Codificación is encoding and does not necessarily conceal information; encryption requires a cryptographic key or equivalent protection mechanism.
example_tl: El cifrado de extremo a extremo protege el contenido de los mensajes, pero no oculta necesariamente quién se comunica ni con qué frecuencia.
example_en: End-to-end encryption protects message content, but it does not necessarily conceal who communicates or how frequently.
cloze: {{c1::El cifrado de extremo a extremo}} protege el contenido de los mensajes, pero no oculta necesariamente quién se comunica ni con qué frecuencia.
note: Old_back is valid rather than erroneous. Self-review selected cifrado as the main term and retained encriptación as a genuine technical alternative.

register: Neutral computing and network-security vocabulary; cortafuegos is the established Spanish equivalent, while firewall remains common among specialists.
trap: Cortafuegos is masculine and has the same written form in singular and plural: el cortafuegos, los cortafuegos.
example_tl: El cortafuegos nacional bloqueó medios extranjeros durante las protestas, pero los ciudadanos siguieron compartiendo copias mediante redes privadas y canales cifrados.
example_en: The national firewall blocked foreign media during the protests, but citizens continued sharing copies through private networks and encrypted channels.
cloze: {{c1::El cortafuegos}} nacional bloqueó medios extranjeros durante las protestas, pero los ciudadanos siguieron compartiendo copias mediante redes privadas y canales cifrados.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the productive non-cognate Spanish term and its invariant plural form.

register: Neutral-formal in statistics, research and algorithmic accountability for a systematic distortion in selection, measurement or outcomes.
trap: Prejuicio is appropriate for a prejudgment or discriminatory attitude, but statistical and algorithmic bias normally requires sesgo.
example_tl: El sesgo de selección distorsionó el estudio porque la muestra excluía a quienes carecían de conexión estable o evitaban las plataformas.
example_en: Selection bias distorted the study because the sample excluded people who lacked a stable connection or avoided the platforms.
cloze: {{c1::El sesgo de selección}} distorsionó el estudio porque la muestra excluía a quienes carecían de conexión estable o evitaban las plataformas.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate but the English prompt is polysemous. The example fixes the statistical sense and separates it from personal prejudice.

register: Neutral technical and policy vocabulary for data describing other data, including communication times, locations, formats or participants.
trap: English metadata often behaves as a mass noun; Spanish normally uses the plural los metadatos, with meta- attached and no hyphen.
example_tl: Los metadatos revelan horarios, ubicaciones y redes de contacto incluso cuando el contenido de las comunicaciones permanece protegido mediante cifrado robusto.
example_en: Metadata reveals times, locations and contact networks even when the content of communications remains protected by strong encryption.
cloze: {{c1::Los metadatos}} revelan horarios, ubicaciones y redes de contacto incluso cuando el contenido de las comunicaciones permanece protegido mediante cifrado robusto.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct but omits the article; the note makes Spanish number and prefix spelling explicit.

register: Neutral-critical for innovation presented as breaking with an established model; disruptivo is established but often carries promotional business-jargon overtones.
trap: English disruptive can also mean perturbador or conflictivo; those senses do not describe an innovation that radically alters an industry or model.
example_tl: La empresa presentó como rupturista una función menor, pero su modelo de negocio seguía dependiendo de publicidad invasiva y extracción masiva de datos.
example_en: The company presented a minor feature as disruptive, but its business model still depended on invasive advertising and mass data extraction.
cloze: La empresa presentó como {{c1::rupturista}} una función menor, pero su modelo de negocio seguía dependiendo de publicidad invasiva y extracción masiva de datos.
note: Old_back is valid in business usage. Self-review chose rupturista as the less promotional main term while preserving disruptivo as an alternative for the intended innovation sense.

register: Learned formal adjective for something present across virtually every place or context; omnipresente is more transparent and broadly used.
trap: The Spanish feminine is ubicua, without an accent; Portuguese ubíqua can prompt the incorrect Spanish spelling *ubícua.
example_tl: La vigilancia ubicua convierte gestos cotidianos en señales comerciales y dificulta que los ciudadanos identifiquen cuándo están siendo observados o evaluados.
example_en: Ubiquitous surveillance turns everyday gestures into commercial signals and makes it difficult for citizens to identify when they are being observed or assessed.
cloze: La vigilancia {{c1::ubicua}} convierte gestos cotidianos en señales comerciales y dificulta que los ciudadanos identifiquen cuándo están siendo observados o evaluados.
note: Old_back supplies only an unexplained feminine form and capitalizes it. The production headword is the masculine lemma ubicuo; the example supplies feminine agreement.

register: Neutral-formal in policy and economic analysis; sin regular is compact, while no regulado is equally natural when modifying a noun.
trap: Desregulado often implies that previous controls were removed; it does not always equal something that has never been regulated.
example_tl: Un mercado sin regular permite que los intermediarios trasladen costes a los usuarios antes de que las autoridades comprendan siquiera el modelo.
example_en: An unregulated market allows intermediaries to pass costs on to users before the authorities even understand the model.
cloze: Un mercado {{c1::sin regular}} permite que los intermediarios trasladen costes a los usuarios antes de que las autoridades comprendan siquiera el modelo.
note: Old_back is valid. Retention is justified by the productive sin + infinitive construction and the important distinction from desregulado.

register: Strongly critical in economic and technology commentary for a model or practice that exploits weaker actors for sustained advantage.
trap: Predatory is stronger than merely competitivo: it implies exploitative conduct aimed at extracting value or eliminating weaker rivals.
example_tl: Un modelo depredador ofrece servicios gratuitos hasta eliminar competidores y después impone comisiones que los comercios pequeños apenas pueden asumir.
example_en: A predatory model offers free services until it eliminates competitors and then imposes fees that small businesses can barely afford.
cloze: Un modelo {{c1::depredador}} ofrece servicios gratuitos hasta eliminar competidores y después impone comisiones que los comercios pequeños apenas pueden asumir.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from capitalization. The example fixes the critical business-practice sense rather than literal animal predation. Self-review removed the broader abusivo alternative because it does not necessarily convey systematic predation.

register: Neutral-formal contemporary adjective, often critical when constant network access is linked to exposure, dependency or information overload.
trap: Spanish uses the prefix hiper-, joined directly to the base without the English y or a hyphen: hiperconectado, not *hyper-conectado.
example_tl: Una sociedad hiperconectada recibe información al instante, pero también multiplica la exposición a campañas coordinadas, rumores virales y episodios de acoso.
example_en: A hyperconnected society receives information instantly, but it also multiplies exposure to coordinated campaigns, viral rumors and episodes of harassment.
cloze: Una sociedad {{c1::hiperconectada}} recibe información al instante, pero también multiplica la exposición a campañas coordinadas, rumores virales y episodios de acoso.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from capitalization. The example supplies feminine agreement while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.

register: Formal political and social-theory adjective, often critical, for an actor or worldview that establishes durable leadership and dominance.
trap: Hegemónico is more specific than merely dominante: in critical theory it can include making a particular worldview appear natural or consensual.
example_tl: El relato hegemónico presenta la extracción masiva de datos como precio inevitable de la innovación y excluye del debate cualquier alternativa regulatoria.
example_en: The hegemonic narrative presents mass data extraction as the inevitable price of innovation and excludes any regulatory alternative from the debate.
cloze: El relato {{c1::hegemónico}} presenta la extracción masiva de datos como precio inevitable de la innovación y excluye del debate cualquier alternativa regulatoria.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the term's specific critical-theory sense rather than by cognate recognition alone.

register: Formal-critical adjective for harm that advances gradually or unobtrusively and is therefore difficult to recognise or resist.
trap: Insidioso does not mean merely peligroso or engañoso; it highlights concealed, gradual harm whose consequences may become visible only later.
example_tl: El efecto insidioso de la personalización consiste en reducir paulatinamente la diversidad informativa sin que el usuario perciba una restricción explícita.
example_en: The insidious effect of personalisation consists in gradually reducing information diversity without the user perceiving an explicit restriction.
cloze: El efecto {{c1::insidioso}} de la personalización consiste en reducir paulatinamente la diversidad informativa sin que el usuario perciba una restricción explícita.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate; the note retains the marked adjective to establish the covert, cumulative component of its meaning.

register: Neutral-formal in literary, cultural and political criticism for a setting or development resembling an oppressive imagined society.
trap: Spanish adapts the English y to i and marks the stress: distópico, not *dystópico or *distopico.
example_tl: El escenario distópico no surge de una máquina omnipotente, sino de miles de decisiones administrativas que convierten la vigilancia en rutina.
example_en: The dystopian scenario does not arise from an omnipotent machine, but from thousands of administrative decisions that turn surveillance into routine.
cloze: El escenario {{c1::distópico}} no surge de una máquina omnipotente, sino de miles de decisiones administrativas que convierten la vigilancia en rutina.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from its failure to expose the Spanish spelling and stress pattern.

register: Neutral technical and policy adjective for a process or system performed through automation rather than direct case-by-case human action.
trap: Automatizado and automático overlap but are not mechanically interchangeable: automatizado emphasises a process converted to automation, as in decisión automatizada.
example_tl: El sistema automatizado rechazó miles de solicitudes porque el modelo heredaba criterios históricos que penalizaban a los barrios con menor renta.
example_en: The automated system rejected thousands of applications because the model inherited historical criteria that penalised lower-income neighbourhoods.
cloze: El sistema {{c1::automatizado}} rechazó miles de solicitudes porque el modelo heredaba criterios históricos que penalizaban a los barrios con menor renta.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. Self-review rejected automático as an alternative because it would blur a useful distinction in automated-decision policy.

register: Neutral-formal in social and policy analysis for a phenomenon distributed broadly across places, systems or everyday practices.
trap: Do not default to penetrante: in abstract policy contexts it can sound physical, whereas generalizado or omnipresente conveys pervasive reach idiomatically.
example_tl: La vigilancia generalizada altera la conducta pública incluso cuando nadie sabe qué datos se recogen, durante cuánto tiempo ni con qué finalidad.
example_en: Pervasive surveillance alters public behaviour even when nobody knows what data is collected, for how long or for what purpose.
cloze: La vigilancia {{c1::generalizada}} altera la conducta pública incluso cuando nadie sabe qué datos se recogen, durante cuánto tiempo ni con qué finalidad.
note: The legacy omnipresente is valid and retained as an alternative; generalizado is the more idiomatic main choice for the policy collocation used here.

register: Learned neutral-formal adjective for something short-lived; fugaz is slightly less elevated and especially natural for attention or success.
trap: Italian effimero may prompt a doubled consonant; Spanish efímero has one f and carries a written accent on í.
example_tl: La atención efímera que generan las campañas virales rara vez sostiene reformas institucionales cuando desaparecen las imágenes que movilizaron al público.
example_en: The ephemeral attention generated by viral campaigns rarely sustains institutional reforms once the images that mobilised the public disappear.
cloze: La atención {{c1::efímera}} que generan las campañas virales rara vez sostiene reformas institucionales cuando desaparecen las imágenes que movilizaron al público.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The example supplies feminine agreement, while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.

register: Formal-analytical construction for an outcome dependent on a stated condition; supeditado a is somewhat more emphatic about subordination.
trap: English contingent on is not normally *contingente en or *contingente sobre; use condicionado a, supeditado a or dependiente de.
example_tl: El acceso al mercado quedó condicionado al cumplimiento de auditorías independientes, no a las promesas voluntarias que la empresa formulaba cada trimestre.
example_en: Market access became contingent on compliance with independent audits, not on the voluntary promises the company made every quarter.
cloze: El acceso al mercado quedó {{c1::condicionado al}} cumplimiento de auditorías independientes, no a las promesas voluntarias que la empresa formulaba cada trimestre.
note: The isolated English prompt is polysemous. This note deliberately selects the high-value contingent-on sense; old_back contingente instead suggests possibility or non-necessity in Spanish.

register: Neutral-critical adjective for a person, message or design that influences others covertly or unfairly for its own ends.
trap: For an agentive design or tactic, manipulador is more idiomatic than simply mirroring English morphology as manipulativo, which is more restricted and technical.
example_tl: El diseño manipulador oculta la opción de rechazar el seguimiento y presenta la aceptación total como si fuera una decisión libre.
example_en: The manipulative design hides the option to reject tracking and presents full acceptance as if it were a free decision.
cloze: El diseño {{c1::manipulador}} oculta la opción de rechazar el seguimiento y presenta la aceptación total como si fuera una decisión libre.
note: Materially refines old_back manipulativo. Self-review selected the ordinary agentive adjective manipulador for the critical design context.

register: Formal-critical in political economy and technology criticism for a model that removes resources, data or value without comparable return.
trap: Extractivo is not automatically equivalent to explotador: the former describes a logic of extraction, while the latter explicitly foregrounds abuse.
example_tl: El modelo extractivo convierte la actividad cotidiana en datos privados y devuelve a las comunidades muy poco del valor económico generado.
example_en: The extractive model turns everyday activity into private data and returns very little of the economic value generated to communities.
cloze: El modelo {{c1::extractivo}} convierte la actividad cotidiana en datos privados y devuelve a las comunidades muy poco del valor económico generado.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. Retention is justified by the productive political-economy metaphor beyond literal resource industries.

register: Strongly critical but standard in analysis when used figuratively for a policy that ignores foreseeable or long-term consequences.
trap: Portuguese míope may prompt a false accent; Spanish miope has no written accent. Cortoplacista fits only when the criticism concerns time horizons.
example_tl: Una política miope subsidia centros de datos sin calcular su consumo hídrico ni la dependencia energética que consolidará durante décadas.
example_en: A myopic policy subsidises data centres without calculating their water consumption or the energy dependence it will entrench for decades.
cloze: Una política {{c1::miope}} subsidia centros de datos sin calcular su consumo hídrico ni la dependencia energética que consolidará durante décadas.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct. The example fixes the figurative policy sense rather than literal short-sightedness.

register: Formal philosophy and intellectual-history adjective referring to Hegel's thought, method or intellectual legacy.
trap: Spanish relational adjectives derived from personal names are normally lowercase: hegeliano, not *Hegeliano; the form also has only one g.
example_tl: El argumento hegeliano interpreta el conflicto como motor del cambio histórico, pero reduce las demandas de actores muy diversos a una síntesis única.
example_en: The Hegelian argument interprets conflict as the engine of historical change, but reduces the demands of very diverse actors to a single synthesis.
cloze: El argumento {{c1::hegeliano}} interpreta el conflicto como motor del cambio histórico, pero reduce las demandas de actores muy diversos a una síntesis única.
note: Corrects the unnecessary capitalisation in old_back; Spanish writes the relational adjective in lowercase. Self-review replaced simplifica actores with a more idiomatic construction.

register: Learned literary and analytical adjective, derived from Proteus, for something that repeatedly changes form, character or position.
trap: Proteico can also be read as relating to proteins; context must establish the Proteus-derived sense of changeability intended by English protean.
example_tl: El discurso proteico del movimiento adopta un lenguaje ecologista, nacionalista o tecnocrático según la audiencia, sin modificar su estructura de poder.
example_en: The movement's protean discourse adopts environmentalist, nationalist or technocratic language depending on the audience, without changing its power structure.
cloze: El discurso {{c1::proteico}} del movimiento adopta un lenguaje ecologista, nacionalista o tecnocrático según la audiencia, sin modificar su estructura de poder.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate but highly marked and polysemous; the note explicitly anchors the intended Proteus-derived sense. Self-review added the article required by the example's enumerated modifiers.

register: Formal analytical adjective for a pattern or result that departs from expectations and may therefore require explanation or investigation.
trap: Spanish writes anómalo with an acute accent; Portuguese anômalo can prompt the wrong accent, while unaccented *anomalo is incorrect.
example_tl: El patrón anómalo de consultas reveló una campaña coordinada, aunque cada cuenta individual parecía respetar los límites formales de la plataforma.
example_en: The anomalous query pattern revealed a coordinated campaign, although each individual account appeared to respect the platform's formal limits.
cloze: El patrón {{c1::anómalo}} de consultas reveló una campaña coordinada, aunque cada cuenta individual parecía respetar los límites formales de la plataforma.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Atípico is retained as a slightly less marked alternative in the same analytical context.

register: Neutral-formal and often emphatic in policy, journalism and historical analysis for something with no known prior equivalent.
trap: The fixed Spanish expression normally uses plural precedentes and no article: sin precedentes; it does not change with the noun's gender or number.
example_tl: La concentración sin precedentes de capacidad informática confiere a pocas empresas una influencia política que las autoridades nacionales apenas pueden contrarrestar.
example_en: The unprecedented concentration of computing capacity gives a few companies political influence that national authorities can barely counteract.
cloze: La concentración {{c1::sin precedentes}} de capacidad informática confiere a pocas empresas una influencia política que las autoridades nacionales apenas pueden contrarrestar.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. The expression is retained because its fixed plural form is a useful nonliteral production target. Self-review changed concede to the more idiomatic confiere una influencia.

register: Formal historical and analytical adjective for a person, document or event existing at the same time as another.
trap: English contemporaneous means co-occurring in time, not necessarily present-day; coetáneo and this sense of contemporáneo normally take a de complement.
example_tl: El informe fue coetáneo de las protestas, pero sus autores ignoraron documentos internos que ya contradecían la versión oficial.
example_en: The report was contemporaneous with the protests, but its authors ignored internal documents that already contradicted the official account.
cloze: El informe fue {{c1::coetáneo de}} las protestas, pero sus autores ignoraron documentos internos que ya contradecían la versión oficial.
note: Materially refines the underdetermined old_back contemporáneo by adding its de complement and blocking the competing present-day sense.

register: Neutral-critical in political and media analysis for conduct, coverage or institutions aligned with a party or faction rather than impartial.
trap: Partidario usually means a supporter and takes de; partisan bias or coverage is partidista, so old_back partidario selects the wrong construction here.
example_tl: La cobertura partidista convirtió una investigación judicial en arma electoral y omitió pruebas que incomodaban tanto al Gobierno como a la oposición.
example_en: Partisan coverage turned a judicial investigation into an electoral weapon and omitted evidence that troubled both the Government and the opposition.
cloze: La cobertura {{c1::partidista}} convirtió una investigación judicial en arma electoral y omitió pruebas que incomodaban tanto al Gobierno como a la oposición.
note: Materially corrects old_back partidario, which denotes a supporter or being in favour of something rather than partisan institutional bias.

register: Strongly critical in labour, economic and platform-policy writing for practices that unfairly profit from weaker actors or their work.
trap: The usual adjective in this abusive sense is explotador, not the literal-looking *explotativo; explotable instead means capable of being exploited.
example_tl: Las condiciones explotadoras obligan a los repartidores a asumir riesgos laborales mientras la plataforma conserva el control sobre tarifas, rutas y sanciones.
example_en: Exploitative conditions force couriers to assume occupational risks while the platform retains control over rates, routes and penalties.
cloze: Las condiciones {{c1::explotadoras}} obligan a los repartidores a asumir riesgos laborales mientras la plataforma conserva el control sobre tarifas, rutas y sanciones.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. The example supplies feminine plural agreement while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.

register: Formal scientific metaphor in political and economic analysis for a close relationship in which the parties sustain or benefit one another.
trap: Simbiótico implies reciprocal dependence or benefit, not mere coexistence; the parties can nevertheless possess very unequal power.
example_tl: La relación simbiótica entre plataformas y partidos amplifica mensajes polarizadores: las primeras obtienen atención y los segundos acceden a audiencias segmentadas.
example_en: The symbiotic relationship between platforms and parties amplifies polarising messages: the former gain attention and the latter access segmented audiences.
cloze: La relación {{c1::simbiótica}} entre plataformas y partidos amplifica mensajes polarizadores: las primeras obtienen atención y los segundos acceden a audiencias segmentadas.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. The example fixes the reciprocal political-economy metaphor and supplies feminine agreement. Self-review replaced potentially ambiguous pronouns with explicit former/latter forms.

register: Neutral-formal adjective for elements that differ markedly in type, origin, scale or character rather than forming a uniform set.
trap: Unlike Portuguese díspar, Spanish dispar and its plural dispares carry no written accent; the plural changes the ending but not the lexeme.
example_tl: El comité reunió fuentes dispares, desde archivos sindicales hasta registros empresariales, y descubrió que todas describían la misma precarización laboral.
example_en: The committee brought together disparate sources, from union archives to company records, and found that all described the same precarisation of labour.
cloze: El comité reunió fuentes {{c1::dispares}}, desde archivos sindicales hasta registros empresariales, y descubrió que todas describían la misma precarización laboral.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the marked adjective, its irregular-looking plural and a genuine Portuguese interference risk.

register: Formal and uncommon in this evaluative sense; it describes a person, tone or attitude that judges others harshly or habitually finds fault.
trap: English censorious concerns severe disapproval, not institutional content removal; Spanish censor here has its older judgmental sense, with feminine censora.
example_tl: La actitud censora del columnista convirtió una discrepancia técnica en falta moral y dejó poco espacio para examinar los argumentos contrarios.
example_en: The columnist's censorious attitude turned a technical disagreement into a moral failing and left little room to examine the opposing arguments.
cloze: La actitud {{c1::censora}} del columnista convirtió una discrepancia técnica en falta moral y dejó poco espacio para examinar los argumentos contrarios.
note: Old_back gives a possible lemma but leaves the rare evaluative sense unspecified. Self-review retained censor only after anchoring harsh judgment and supplying feminine morphology.

register: Neutral-formal legal and policy term; its precise statutory scope varies across legal systems.
trap: In Spanish law, propiedad intelectual often refers specifically to copyright and related rights, while patents and trademarks fall under propiedad industrial.
example_tl: El acuerdo exige proteger la propiedad intelectual, pero distingue los derechos de autor de las patentes sobre tecnologías desarrolladas con fondos públicos.
example_en: The agreement requires intellectual property to be protected, but distinguishes copyright from patents on technologies developed with public funds.
cloze: El acuerdo exige proteger {{c1::la propiedad intelectual}}, pero distingue los derechos de autor de las patentes sobre tecnologías desarrolladas con fondos públicos.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct but conceals a material legal-system difference: Spanish propiedad intelectual may be narrower than the English umbrella term.

register: Neutral business, logistics and industrial-policy term; cadena de suministro is the usual choice in Spain.
trap: Portuguese cadeia de suprimentos can prompt the non-Spanish calque *cadena de suprimentos; use cadena de suministro or cadena de abastecimiento.
example_tl: La crisis reveló que la cadena de suministro europea dependía de pocos fabricantes asiáticos para componentes esenciales de redes y centros de datos.
example_en: The crisis revealed that the European supply chain depended on a small number of Asian manufacturers for essential network and data-centre components.
cloze: La crisis reveló que {{c1::la cadena de suministro}} europea dependía de pocos fabricantes asiáticos para componentes esenciales de redes y centros de datos.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Cadena de abastecimiento is retained as a genuine alternative, especially common in Latin American usage.

register: Neutral-formal trade and customs vocabulary for a duty imposed on imported or exported goods.
trap: English tariff is not always tarifa: a customs duty is an arancel, whereas tarifa normally denotes a price schedule or service charge.
example_tl: Los aranceles sobre componentes electrónicos encarecieron la producción nacional sin crear proveedores alternativos, porque las empresas siguieron dependiendo de maquinaria importada.
example_en: Tariffs on electronic components made domestic production more expensive without creating alternative suppliers, because companies remained dependent on imported machinery.
cloze: {{c1::Los aranceles sobre}} componentes electrónicos encarecieron la producción nacional sin crear proveedores alternativos, porque las empresas siguieron dependiendo de maquinaria importada.
note: The legacy plural is correct; the production headword restores the singular lemma and its productive sobre complement.

register: Formal economic and geopolitical vocabulary for deliberately reducing strategic interdependence between countries, sectors or technological systems.
trap: Desacoplamiento is stronger than reducción de riesgos: the latter can preserve substantial ties while diversifying selected strategic dependencies.
example_tl: El desacoplamiento avanza de forma selectiva: los gobiernos restringen chips estratégicos mientras preservan intercambios comerciales que consideran menos sensibles.
example_en: Decoupling is advancing selectively: governments restrict strategic chips while preserving trade flows that they consider less sensitive.
cloze: {{c1::El desacoplamiento}} avanza de forma selectiva: los gobiernos restringen chips estratégicos mientras preservan intercambios comerciales que consideran menos sensibles.
note: The legacy desvinculación is valid and retained as an alternative; desacoplamiento is the established main term in current geoeconomic debate.

register: Formal-critical political and geopolitical vocabulary for improper involvement in another actor's affairs or processes.
trap: Interferencia is natural for signals, waves or operational disruption; improper political interference is more idiomatically injerencia or intromisión.
example_tl: La injerencia en procesos electorales no siempre altera el recuento; también puede erosionar la confianza pública mediante filtraciones selectivas y campañas encubiertas.
example_en: Interference in electoral processes does not always alter the count; it can also erode public confidence through selective leaks and covert campaigns.
cloze: {{c1::La injerencia en}} procesos electorales no siempre altera el recuento; también puede erosionar la confianza pública mediante filtraciones selectivas y campañas encubiertas.
note: The isolated English prompt is polysemous. This note deliberately selects political interference and materially replaces legacy interferencia, which suggests a technical sense here.

register: Formal institutional usage; normativa denotes a body of applicable rules, while regulación can denote either that framework or the activity of regulating.
trap: Reglamentación is possible but often foregrounds detailed implementing rules; English plural regulations is frequently the collective Spanish singular normativa.
example_tl: La normativa europea exige que las plataformas expliquen sus sistemas de recomendación y ofrezcan a los investigadores acceso seguro a ciertos datos.
example_en: European regulations require platforms to explain their recommendation systems and give researchers secure access to certain data.
cloze: {{c1::La normativa}} europea exige que las plataformas expliquen sus sistemas de recomendación y ofrezcan a los investigadores acceso seguro a ciertos datos.
note: Materially refines old_back reglamentación by selecting the idiomatic collective noun for a body of binding rules in this institutional context.

register: Formal competition-law and market-policy expression for economic power that lets an undertaking behave substantially independently of competitors or customers.
trap: Generic dominio does not supply the established competition-law collocation; abuse of dominance is abuso de posición dominante, not *abuso de dominancia.
example_tl: La posición dominante de la plataforma le permite imponer comisiones a los desarrolladores sin negociar condiciones ni ofrecer mecanismos eficaces de apelación.
example_en: The platform's dominant position allows it to impose fees on developers without negotiating terms or offering effective appeal mechanisms.
cloze: {{c1::La posición dominante}} de la plataforma le permite imponer comisiones a los desarrolladores sin negociar condiciones ni ofrecer mecanismos eficaces de apelación.
note: The prompt is polysemous. This note selects the high-value competition-policy sense and replaces legacy dominio with its established legal collocation.

register: Neutral specialist vocabulary; computación cuántica and informática cuántica are both established in Spain's technical and policy writing.
trap: The field is computación cuántica, whereas a physical device is an ordenador cuántico or computador cuántico; the terms are related but not interchangeable.
example_tl: La computación cuántica aún no amenaza todo el cifrado existente, pero obliga a adoptar estándares criptográficos poscuánticos antes de que maduren los equipos.
example_en: Quantum computing does not yet threaten all existing encryption, but it makes it necessary to adopt post-quantum cryptographic standards before the machines mature.
cloze: {{c1::La computación cuántica}} aún no amenaza todo el cifrado existente, pero obliga a adoptar estándares criptográficos poscuánticos antes de que maduren los equipos.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Informática cuántica is retained as a natural Spain-oriented alternative. Self-review replaced the vague estándares resistentes with the established estándares criptográficos poscuánticos.

register: Neutral technical and institutional usage for agreed specifications governing compatibility, quality or implementation.
trap: Portuguese padrões must not become Spanish *padrones, which means registers or censuses; use estándares or normas according to context.
example_tl: Los estándares técnicos abiertos reducen la dependencia de un proveedor y permiten que administraciones distintas intercambien datos sin adoptar sistemas idénticos.
example_en: Open technical standards reduce dependence on one supplier and allow different public administrations to exchange data without adopting identical systems.
cloze: {{c1::Los estándares técnicos}} abiertos reducen la dependencia de un proveedor y permiten que administraciones distintas intercambien datos sin adoptar sistemas idénticos.
note: Legacy normas is valid and retained in the more precise alternative normas técnicas; estándares técnicos is especially idiomatic for interoperability specifications.

register: Standard institutional, academic and business abbreviation in Spain for investigación y desarrollo; often expanded on first mention in formal documents.
trap: Spanish retains neither English R&D nor Portuguese P&D in domestic usage: the conventional abbreviation is I+D and is feminine through investigación.
example_tl: La I+D pública puede orientar proyectos arriesgados hacia objetivos sociales que el capital privado descarta por prometer rendimientos demasiado tardíos o inciertos.
example_en: Public R&D can direct risky projects towards social goals that private capital rejects because they promise returns that are too delayed or uncertain.
cloze: {{c1::La I+D}} pública puede orientar proyectos arriesgados hacia objetivos sociales que el capital privado descarta por prometer rendimientos demasiado tardíos o inciertos.
note: The legacy equivalent is correct, but the production note adds the conventional feminine article and removes unnecessary capitalization from the expansion. Self-review replaced the calque retornos lentos with rendimientos tardíos.

register: Formal technology-policy term for the capacity of a polity or institution to govern its digital infrastructure, data and strategic dependencies.
trap: Soberanía digital does not necessarily mean complete technological self-sufficiency; it can instead concern regulatory control, auditability and substitutable suppliers.
example_tl: La soberanía digital no exige fabricar cada componente dentro de Europa, sino conservar la capacidad política para auditar, sustituir y regular proveedores.
example_en: Digital sovereignty does not require manufacturing every component within Europe, but rather retaining the political capacity to audit, replace and regulate suppliers.
cloze: {{c1::La soberanía digital}} no exige fabricar cada componente dentro de Europa, sino conservar la capacidad política para auditar, sustituir y regular proveedores.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Retention is justified by the term's contested policy meaning rather than cognate recognition alone. Self-review restored the article in la capacidad política for idiomatic flow.

register: Standard legal and policy term in Spain and the EU for rules and practices governing the lawful processing of personal data.
trap: Protección de datos names the regulatory field; privacidad de los datos can denote the protected interest, so the two expressions do not always coincide.
example_tl: La protección de datos exige limitar la recogida de información, incluso cuando cada usuario haya aceptado formalmente una política de privacidad extensa.
example_en: Data privacy requires limiting information collection, even when each user has formally accepted an extensive policy governing personal information.
cloze: {{c1::La protección de datos}} exige limitar la recogida de información, incluso cuando cada usuario haya aceptado formalmente una política de privacidad extensa.
note: Materially replaces legacy privacidad de los datos by selecting the institutional EU-policy sense established by the example; the more literal phrase remains valid in other contexts.

register: Formal US legal and historical proper name; the year identifies the federal statute rather than espionage legislation in general.
trap: English Act in the title is ley, not acto; Spanish capitalizes Ley and Espionaje when they form the translated identifying name of this statute.
example_tl: La Ley de Espionaje de 1917 se ha invocado contra responsables de filtraciones, aunque sus defensores sostienen que protege secretos esenciales para la seguridad nacional.
example_en: The Espionage Act of 1917 has been invoked against those responsible for leaks, although its defenders argue that it protects secrets essential to national security.
cloze: {{c1::La Ley de Espionaje de 1917}} se ha invocado contra responsables de filtraciones, aunque sus defensores sostienen que protege secretos esenciales para la seguridad nacional.
note: The legacy title is broadly correct but underspecified; adding de 1917 anchors the intended US statute and prevents a generic reading.

register: Neutral technical and technology-policy usage; informática en la nube is also natural in Spain.
trap: Cloud is rendered with an en phrase: computación en la nube or informática en la nube, not an English-patterned compound such as *computación nube.
example_tl: La computación en la nube permitió ampliar rápidamente la capacidad del servicio, pero concentró datos sensibles en infraestructuras sometidas a jurisdicciones extranjeras.
example_en: Cloud computing allowed the service's capacity to be expanded rapidly, but concentrated sensitive data in infrastructure subject to foreign jurisdictions.
cloze: {{c1::La computación en la nube}} permitió ampliar rápidamente la capacidad del servicio, pero concentró datos sensibles en infraestructuras sometidas a jurisdicciones extranjeras.
note: The legacy computación en nube is valid; the main form adds the definite article, which is especially natural in general professional prose. Self-review replaced the technical anglicism escalar el servicio with ampliar la capacidad del servicio.

register: Neutral specialist networking term; the international abbreviation IP is retained from English and is widely used after expansion.
trap: El protocolo IP is not la dirección IP: the protocol defines packet addressing and routing, while an IP address identifies an interface within that scheme.
example_tl: El protocolo de internet permite que redes heterogéneas intercambien paquetes, pero no garantiza por sí mismo la confidencialidad ni la autenticidad.
example_en: The Internet Protocol allows heterogeneous networks to exchange packets, but does not by itself guarantee confidentiality or authenticity.
cloze: {{c1::El protocolo de internet}} permite que redes heterogéneas intercambien paquetes, pero no garantiza por sí mismo la confidencialidad ni la autenticidad.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct but uses unnecessary title-style capitals; contemporary Spanish normally writes the common nouns in lowercase.

register: Specialist cybersecurity term for an access model that continually verifies identities, devices and requests instead of trusting network location.
trap: Confianza cero is not ordinary interpersonal distrust; in security it labels a verification architecture, so the bare legacy phrase needs a head noun.
example_tl: El modelo de confianza cero parte de que ninguna identidad debe recibir acceso permanente y exige verificar cada solicitud según su contexto y riesgo.
example_en: The zero-trust model assumes that no identity should receive permanent access and requires every request to be verified according to its context and risk.
cloze: {{c1::El modelo de confianza cero}} parte de que ninguna identidad debe recibir acceso permanente y exige verificar cada solicitud según su contexto y riesgo.
note: Materially refines old_back confianza cero by supplying the domain head noun needed for a production-ready Spanish term. Self-review replaced the anthropomorphic merece acceso with debe recibir acceso.

register: Neutral scientific and semiconductor-industry term for the chemical element used as the substrate in most integrated circuits.
trap: English silicon is silicio; silicona means silicone, the family of synthetic polymers used in sealants, implants and other products.
example_tl: El silicio sigue siendo esencial para fabricar chips avanzados, aunque la ventaja competitiva depende también del diseño, la maquinaria y el encapsulado.
example_en: Silicon remains essential for manufacturing advanced chips, although competitive advantage also depends on design, machinery and packaging.
cloze: {{c1::El silicio}} sigue siendo esencial para fabricar chips avanzados, aunque la ventaja competitiva depende también del diseño, la maquinaria y el encapsulado.
note: The legacy rendering is correct. Retention is justified by the consequential silicon/silicone false-friend distinction.

register: Specialist semiconductor-manufacturing term for the thin disc on which many integrated circuits are fabricated before separation.
trap: Oblea also denotes a thin edible wafer; semiconductor context or a modifier such as semiconductora or de silicio is needed to fix the technical sense.
example_tl: La oblea semiconductora atraviesa cientos de procesos antes de dividirse en chips, por lo que un defecto microscópico puede reducir mucho el rendimiento.
example_en: The semiconductor wafer goes through hundreds of processes before being divided into chips, so a microscopic defect can greatly reduce the yield.
cloze: {{c1::La oblea semiconductora}} atraviesa cientos de procesos antes de dividirse en chips, por lo que un defecto microscópico puede reducir mucho el rendimiento.
note: The legacy oblea is correct but polysemous; the production headword adds semiconductora to anchor the intended technical sense.

register: Specialist semiconductor-industry term for a facility or business that manufactures chips designed by other companies.
trap: Without a domain modifier, fundición normally suggests a metal foundry; de semiconductores fixes the contract-manufacturing sense intended here.
example_tl: La fundición de semiconductores reservará parte de su capacidad para diseñadores europeos, aunque seguirá dependiendo de maquinaria litográfica importada.
example_en: The semiconductor foundry will reserve part of its capacity for European designers, although it will remain dependent on imported lithography equipment.
cloze: {{c1::La fundición de semiconductores}} reservará parte de su capacidad para diseñadores europeos, aunque seguirá dependiendo de maquinaria litográfica importada.
note: The legacy fundición is possible but too ambiguous as a production headword; the domain complement follows Spanish EU semiconductor-policy usage.

register: Specialist microfabrication term for transferring circuit patterns onto a light-sensitive wafer surface.
trap: Bare litografía also denotes artistic and printing processes; fotolitografía anchors the light-based semiconductor-manufacturing sense.
example_tl: La fotolitografía proyecta patrones diminutos sobre la oblea, y cualquier desviación en la exposición puede inutilizar miles de circuitos antes del encapsulado.
example_en: Photolithography projects minute patterns onto the wafer, and any deviation in exposure can render thousands of circuits unusable before packaging.
cloze: {{c1::La fotolitografía}} proyecta patrones diminutos sobre la oblea, y cualquier desviación en la exposición puede inutilizar miles de circuitos antes del encapsulado.
note: The legacy litografía is a valid hypernym but underspecifies the process selected by the semiconductor context.

register: Specialist microelectronics term for an individual piece cut from a processed wafer before or during packaging.
trap: English die is highly polysemous: matriz denotes a mould or stamping die, not the semiconductor component intended in this batch.
example_tl: Cada pastilla semiconductora se prueba antes del encapsulado para evitar que un defecto microscópico encarezca el montaje del procesador completo.
example_en: Each semiconductor die is tested before packaging to prevent a microscopic defect from making assembly of the complete processor more expensive.
cloze: Cada {{c1::pastilla semiconductora}} se prueba antes del encapsulado para evitar que un defecto microscópico encarezca el montaje del procesador completo.
note: Materially corrects old_back matriz. Spanish technical and regulatory texts use pastilla semiconductora; chip sin encapsular is retained as a transparent alternative.

tl: la empresa de semiconductores sin fábrica
register: Neutral-formal industrial-policy expression; the specialist anglicism fabless is also common, postnominal and invariable.
trap: Fabless does not mean that a business lacks offices: it designs or markets semiconductors while outsourcing their physical fabrication.
example_tl: La empresa de semiconductores sin fábrica conserva el diseño y la comercialización, pero encarga la producción a una fundición especializada.
example_en: The fabless semiconductor company retains design and marketing, but entrusts production to a specialist foundry.
cloze: {{c1::La empresa de semiconductores sin fábrica}} conserva el diseño y la comercialización, pero encarga la producción a una fundición especializada.
note: The source English is an awkward nominalization but still identifies a valuable industry model. The production headword replaces unusable legacy el Fabless.

alts: el sistema integrado en un chip (SoC)
register: Specialist electronics term; Spanish technical prose commonly introduces the international abbreviation SoC after the expanded form.
trap: A system on a chip is not merely a microprocessor: it integrates several functional components, and Spanish normally requires un in en un chip.
example_tl: El sistema en un chip (SoC) integra procesador, memoria y comunicaciones, lo que reduce el consumo energético de dispositivos pequeños y conectados.
example_en: The system on a chip (SoC) integrates a processor, memory and communications, reducing the energy consumption of small connected devices.
cloze: {{c1::El sistema en un chip (SoC)}} integra procesador, memoria y comunicaciones, lo que reduce el consumo energético de dispositivos pequeños y conectados.
note: Materially refines old_back Sistema en Chip by restoring the article, normalizing lowercase and supplying the established abbreviation.

register: Standard technical and academic term; the English label remains common in specialist settings but is unnecessary in general Spanish prose.
trap: Deep learning is a family of machine-learning methods, not a synonym for any sophisticated learning process; profundo is the established modifier.
example_tl: El aprendizaje profundo mejoró la detección de tumores, pero sus resultados variaban entre hospitales por diferencias en los datos clínicos disponibles.
example_en: Deep learning improved tumour detection, but its results varied between hospitals because of differences in the clinical data available.
cloze: {{c1::El aprendizaje profundo}} mejoró la detección de tumores, pero sus resultados variaban entre hospitales por diferencias en los datos clínicos disponibles.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate; the production headword adds the article and uses normal Spanish lowercase styling.

register: Standard Spanish technical and policy term; the English label is frequent in industry but less suitable in nonspecialist formal prose.
trap: Portuguese aprendizagem de máquina can prompt the calque aprendizaje de máquina; in Spain, aprendizaje automático is the established general term.
example_tl: El aprendizaje automático permite detectar operaciones fraudulentas, aunque un modelo mal evaluado puede reproducir sesgos presentes en los historiales bancarios.
example_en: Machine learning makes it possible to detect fraudulent transactions, although a poorly evaluated model can reproduce biases present in banking records.
cloze: {{c1::El aprendizaje automático}} permite detectar operaciones fraudulentas, aunque un modelo mal evaluado puede reproducir sesgos presentes en los historiales bancarios.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate. Retention is justified by the conventional nonliteral Spanish field name and the cross-language interference risk.

alts: los datos para entrenar el modelo
register: Neutral specialist machine-learning term for data used to fit a model's parameters.
trap: Conjunto de entrenamiento denotes a training set, usually a defined subset; it is not automatically interchangeable with all training data.
example_tl: Los datos de entrenamiento excluían varios dialectos, por lo que el asistente transcribía peor a quienes se alejaban de la norma peninsular.
example_en: The training data excluded several dialects, so the assistant transcribed speakers who departed from the peninsular norm less accurately.
cloze: {{c1::Los datos de entrenamiento}} excluían varios dialectos, por lo que el asistente transcribía peor a quienes se alejaban de la norma peninsular.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate; the note fixes the intended model-training sense and avoids unnecessary capitalization.

register: Specialist computing term; PLN is the Spanish abbreviation, although the English abbreviation NLP also appears in multilingual professional settings.
trap: The field concerns human language, but lenguaje natural is the established term; do not replace it mechanically with *idioma natural.
example_tl: El procesamiento del lenguaje natural (PLN) permite analizar millones de comentarios, pero los modelos todavía confunden ironía, ambigüedad y referencias culturales locales.
example_en: Natural language processing (NLP) makes it possible to analyse millions of comments, but models still confuse irony, ambiguity and local cultural references.
cloze: {{c1::El procesamiento del lenguaje natural (PLN)}} permite analizar millones de comentarios, pero los modelos todavía confunden ironía, ambigüedad y referencias culturales locales.
note: The legacy words are broadly correct but use title-style capitals and omit the useful Spanish abbreviation PLN. Self-review replaced a compressed facilitar + infinitive construction and gave confunden an explicit subject.

register: Specialist machine-learning term; the English-derived abbreviation GAN is normally retained after a Spanish expansion.
trap: Portuguese redes adversárias generativas can pull the adjectives into that order; established Spanish usage commonly has generativas before adversarias.
example_tl: Las redes generativas adversarias (GAN) pueden producir imágenes convincentes, pero también amplifican errores cuando el conjunto de entrenamiento representa mal a la población.
example_en: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) can produce convincing images, but they also amplify errors when the training set poorly represents the population.
cloze: {{c1::Las redes generativas adversarias (GAN)}} pueden producir imágenes convincentes, pero también amplifican errores cuando el conjunto de entrenamiento representa mal a la población.
note: Terminology varies across Spanish technical writing. The note selects the well-attested redes generativas adversarias; legacy adversariales occurs but is not the preferred form here.

register: Standard technical term for learning through actions, rewards and penalties within an environment.
trap: The established construction is por refuerzo; aprendizaje reforzado would describe learning that has been strengthened rather than name this method.
example_tl: El aprendizaje por refuerzo permitió optimizar el consumo del centro de datos, aunque la recompensa inicial favorecía decisiones eficientes pero difíciles de auditar.
example_en: Reinforcement learning made it possible to optimize the data centre's consumption, although the initial reward favoured efficient decisions that were difficult to audit.
cloze: {{c1::El aprendizaje por refuerzo}} permitió optimizar el consumo del centro de datos, aunque la recompensa inicial favorecía decisiones eficientes pero difíciles de auditar.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate; the production headword restores the article and normal Spanish lowercase styling.

register: Neutral-formal business and supply-chain vocabulary; public procurement is instead contratación pública in Spanish institutional usage.
trap: Procurement is context-sensitive: contratación suits public tendering, whereas aprovisionamiento covers securing the goods and inputs an organization needs.
example_tl: El aprovisionamiento centralizado redujo costes, pero dejó a las filiales atadas a un proveedor incapaz de ajustar sus entregas a necesidades locales.
example_en: Centralized procurement reduced costs, but left the subsidiaries tied to a supplier unable to adjust its deliveries to local needs.
cloze: {{c1::El aprovisionamiento}} centralizado redujo costes, pero dejó a las filiales atadas a un proveedor incapaz de ajustar sus entregas a necesidades locales.
note: The prompt is polysemous. This note selects the private-sector supply-chain sense represented by legacy aprovisionamiento and distinguishes public procurement explicitly. Self-review replaced services with deliveries to keep the example within that selected logistics sense.

register: Specialist production and inventory-management term; JIT is widely understood after the Spanish expansion.
trap: Justo a tiempo is also an everyday adverbial meaning on time; adding sistema or producción identifies the inventory method rather than the ordinary phrase.
example_tl: El sistema justo a tiempo (JIT) redujo inventarios durante años, pero mostró su fragilidad cuando los cierres portuarios interrumpieron entregas esenciales.
example_en: The just-in-time (JIT) system reduced inventories for years, but revealed its fragility when port closures disrupted essential deliveries.
cloze: {{c1::El sistema justo a tiempo (JIT)}} redujo inventarios durante años, pero mostró su fragilidad cuando los cierres portuarios interrumpieron entregas esenciales.
note: Materially refines the underspecified legacy phrase by adding a domain head noun, the standard abbreviation and lowercase Spanish styling.

register: Specialist supply-chain term for logistics functions performed by an external provider; the international abbreviation 3PL is common.
trap: Third party is tercero in this commercial relationship, not *tercer partido, which evokes political parties or parties to a game.
example_tl: La logística de terceros (3PL) permitió abrir nuevos mercados sin construir almacenes propios, aunque dificultó supervisar los retrasos y gestionar las devoluciones.
example_en: Third-party logistics (3PL) enabled entry into new markets without building warehouses, although it complicated monitoring delays and managing returns.
cloze: {{c1::La logística de terceros (3PL)}} permitió abrir nuevos mercados sin construir almacenes propios, aunque dificultó supervisar los retrasos y gestionar las devoluciones.
note: The legacy equivalent is essentially correct; the production note normalizes lowercase and adds the established abbreviation. Self-review replaced the calque visibilidad sobre with idiomatic verbal coordination.

register: Neutral-formal logistics term for the elapsed time from an order or commitment to delivery; other stages may require a more specific modifier.
trap: Lead does not mean liderazgo here. Depending on the measured process, lead time can also be plazo de fabricación or plazo de aprovisionamiento.
example_tl: El plazo de entrega aumentó en tres semanas porque el proveedor no había reservado capacidad suficiente para atender el repunte de pedidos.
example_en: The lead time increased by three weeks because the supplier had not reserved enough capacity to meet the surge in orders.
cloze: {{c1::El plazo de entrega}} aumentó en tres semanas porque el proveedor no había reservado capacidad suficiente para atender el repunte de pedidos.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate for the customer-facing logistics sense; the register line records the source term's process-dependent variation. Self-review restored en in the measure-of-change construction.

tl: la búsqueda y selección de proveedores
register: Neutral-formal business expression for identifying, evaluating and selecting suppliers; specialists also use the English anglicism sourcing.
trap: Sourcing is narrower than procurement: it focuses on finding and choosing supply sources, while procurement also covers purchasing and contract administration.
example_tl: La búsqueda y selección de proveedores incorporó criterios climáticos y laborales, de modo que el precio dejó de decidir por sí solo.
example_en: Supplier sourcing incorporated climate and labour criteria, so price ceased to be the sole deciding factor.
cloze: {{c1::La búsqueda y selección de proveedores}} incorporó criterios climáticos y laborales, de modo que el precio dejó de decidir por sí solo.
note: Materially replaces old_back aprovisionamiento, which blurs the useful distinction between supplier selection and the broader procurement process.

register: Standard retail and inventory-management expression in Spain; the English abbreviation SKU is retained and usually pronounced as individual letters.
trap: An SKU is an internal company reference, not a universal EAN or GTIN; different businesses may assign different SKUs to the same product.
example_tl: Cada referencia interna (SKU) distingue talla y color, de modo que el comercio puede reponer una variante sin confundirla con productos similares.
example_en: Each stock keeping unit (SKU) distinguishes size and colour, allowing the retailer to replenish one variant without confusing it with similar products.
cloze: Cada {{c1::referencia interna (SKU)}} distingue talla y color, de modo que el comercio puede reponer una variante sin confundirla con productos similares.
note: Materially replaces the literal and unnatural legacy Unidad de Mantenimiento de Existencias with the Spain-oriented retail term referencia interna.

register: Neutral-formal economics and supply-chain term; previsión is especially natural in Spain, while pronóstico is also established.
trap: Do not confuse previsión, a forecast, with provisión, the act or result of providing; Portuguese previsão can also prompt a non-Spanish nasal spelling.
example_tl: La previsión de la demanda subestimó las ventas rurales porque el modelo extrapoló hábitos urbanos y apenas incorporó información sobre cobertura móvil.
example_en: Demand forecasting underestimated rural sales because the model extrapolated urban habits and incorporated very little information about mobile coverage.
cloze: {{c1::La previsión de la demanda}} subestimó las ventas rurales porque el modelo extrapoló hábitos urbanos y apenas incorporó información sobre cobertura móvil.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate; the production note normalizes lowercase and records the Spain-oriented choice over pronóstico.

register: Specialist supply-chain term for increasing demand variability as orders move upstream from retailers to producers and suppliers.
trap: The established compound is efecto látigo, without de; it denotes amplified order fluctuations, not merely a sudden disruption in supply.
example_tl: El efecto látigo convirtió una variación modesta de las ventas en pedidos excesivos, inventarios sobrantes y oscilaciones cada vez mayores conforme avanzaba hacia los proveedores.
example_en: The bullwhip effect turned a modest variation in sales into excessive orders, surplus inventories and increasingly large fluctuations as it moved towards suppliers.
cloze: {{c1::El efecto látigo}} convirtió una variación modesta de las ventas en pedidos excesivos, inventarios sobrantes y oscilaciones cada vez mayores conforme avanzaba hacia los proveedores.
note: The legacy term is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Retention is justified by the fixed metaphor and its precise supply-chain meaning. Self-review replaced an implausible reference to successive stoppages with the defining upstream amplification.

register: Neutral-formal business and public-administration term in Spain for transferring an internal function to an outside provider.
trap: Subcontratación overlaps but need not transfer a formerly internal function; Latin American tercerización is not the preferred Spain-oriented headword here.
example_tl: La externalización del servicio redujo costes inmediatos, pero dispersó responsabilidades y dificultó que la administración recuperase conocimiento técnico propio.
example_en: Outsourcing the service reduced immediate costs, but dispersed responsibilities and made it harder for the administration to recover its own technical expertise.
cloze: {{c1::La externalización del}} servicio redujo costes inmediatos, pero dispersó responsabilidades y dificultó que la administración recuperase conocimiento técnico propio.
note: The legacy equivalent is accurate; the production headword adds the governed de complement and the example supplies its contracted form del.

register: Neutral-formal logistics term for organizing warehouse operations, including receipt, placement, picking and dispatch.
trap: Almacenamiento can denote storage alone; warehousing often names the broader operation and management of warehouses and their material flows.
example_tl: La gestión de almacenes automatizada aceleró los pedidos, pero los fallos del sistema bloquearon simultáneamente la recepción, la preparación y la expedición.
example_en: Automated warehousing sped up orders, but system failures simultaneously blocked receiving, picking and dispatch.
cloze: {{c1::La gestión de almacenes}} automatizada aceleró los pedidos, pero los fallos del sistema bloquearon simultáneamente la recepción, la preparación y la expedición.
note: Materially refines legacy almacenamiento by selecting the broader operational sense of warehousing fixed by the batch's supply-chain context.

register: Neutral business and administrative construction for following status or progress; rastrear is narrower and foregrounds locating or tracing a path.
trap: Avoid the unnecessary anglicism trackear; in Spain the fixed construction is hacer el seguimiento de, with de before its object.
example_tl: La empresa hace el seguimiento de cada envío para detectar pronto cualquier desvío, pero no comunica al cliente todas las incidencias registradas.
example_en: The company tracks every shipment to detect any deviation early, but does not inform the customer of every recorded incident.
cloze: La empresa {{c1::hace el seguimiento de}} cada envío para detectar pronto cualquier desvío, pero no comunica al cliente todas las incidencias registradas.
note: Materially refines old_back rastrear, which is valid for tracing or locating but too narrow for routine operational status tracking. Self-review replaced the unnatural collocation desvíos tempranos with detectar pronto cualquier desvío.

register: Beneficiarse de is neutral and broad; lucrarse con is more critical and often suggests questionable gain.
trap: Rentabilizar is transitive and means to make something profitable; intransitive profit is beneficiarse de or obtener beneficios de.
example_tl: Varias consultoras se beneficiaron de la crisis al vender sistemas de vigilancia cuya eficacia nunca fue evaluada por organismos independientes.
example_en: Several consultancies profited from the crisis by selling surveillance systems whose effectiveness was never evaluated by independent bodies.
cloze: Varias consultoras {{c1::se beneficiaron de}} la crisis al vender sistemas de vigilancia cuya eficacia nunca fue evaluada por organismos independientes.
note: Materially corrects legacy rentabilizar, which reverses the argument structure and would mean making the crisis or another object profitable.

register: Neutral-formal in privacy, research and institutional writing; recopilar datos is an equally standard alternative.
trap: English collect does not always mean recoger: for deliberately gathering information, recabar or recopilar datos is more precise; the infinitive itself takes no para.
example_tl: Las plataformas recaban datos de navegación incluso antes de que el usuario inicie sesión, lo que dificulta atribuir responsabilidades entre empresas.
example_en: Platforms collect browsing data even before the user signs in, which makes it difficult to assign responsibility among companies.
cloze: Las plataformas {{c1::recaban datos}} de navegación incluso antes de que el usuario inicie sesión, lo que dificulta atribuir responsabilidades entre empresas.
note: Materially replaces old_back para recoger: para incorrectly translates the English infinitive marker, while recoger is less precise for purposeful data collection.

register: Neutral and widely usable; anunciar is more compact, while publicitar is common in commercial and marketing language.
trap: Do not confuse advertise with advertir: Spanish advertir normally means to warn or notice, not to promote a product or service.
example_tl: Las plataformas hacen publicidad de sus servicios como espacios abiertos, aunque sus normas internas favorecen sistemáticamente a quienes pueden pagar mayor visibilidad.
example_en: Platforms advertise their services as open spaces, although their internal rules systematically favour those who can pay for greater visibility.
cloze: Las plataformas {{c1::hacen publicidad de}} sus servicios como espacios abiertos, aunque sus normas internas favorecen sistemáticamente a quienes pueden pagar mayor visibilidad.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate; the production headword adds the governed de complement and avoids an English-Spanish false friend.

alts: tratar a alguien de forma discriminatoria
register: Neutral-formal in legal, institutional and social-policy discussion; the construction explicitly identifies both the affected person and the grounds.
trap: In the unequal-treatment sense, a human direct object takes personal a and the grounds normally follow por; neutral differentiation may instead require distinguir.
example_tl: El sistema discriminaba a solicitantes por su código postal, pues la variable territorial reproducía desigualdades que el proveedor nunca había evaluado.
example_en: The system discriminated against applicants on the basis of their postcode, since the geographical variable reproduced inequalities that the provider had never assessed.
cloze: El sistema {{c1::discriminaba}} {{c1::a}} solicitantes {{c1::por}} su código postal, pues la variable territorial reproducía desigualdades que el proveedor nunca había evaluado.
note: The legacy cognate is correct but omits the argument structure that makes the verb production-ready.

register: Formal legal and policy usage; conculcar is more elevated and emphatic than the neutral-formal vulnerar.
